post_understanding.summary: A MySQL INNER JOIN with GROUP BY on a large fact table (13.7M rows) joined to a small dimension table (334 rows) takes ~30 seconds. EXPLAIN shows scanning the country_detail index and probing statistic_detail via an index, leading to many index lookups and effectively touching most rows in the large table.
symptoms: large table involved in join (13,731,253 rows)
EXPLAIN shows index scan on small table and ref on large table
no explicit temporary/filesort shown in EXPLAIN
suspected_root_causes: suboptimal join order/plan causing nested-loop expansion over most of the 13.7M rows
GROUP BY after join prevents early de-duplication, forcing many index reads
cold buffer pool or I/O-bound access on first run
high per-row cost due to utf8mb4 string comparisons on join keys
key_evidence: Query: SELECT country_detail.country_name FROM statistic_detail INNER JOIN country_detail ON statistic_detail.country = country_detail.country_code GROUP BY 1
statistic_detail has 13731253 rows; country_detail has 334 rows
EXPLAIN shows: country_detail type=index using country_name_idx; statistic_detail type=ref using an index on country (key_len 82); Extra: Using index; Using where
assumptions: DBMS is MySQL/InnoDB (syntax and EXPLAIN format indicate MySQL 5.7/8.0).
Both tables use default utf8mb4 collation and compatible collations (no implicit conversions).
Optimizer chooses country_detail as the driving table and statistic_detail via ref lookup as shown.
Distribution of statistic_detail.country values spans most/all 334 country codes (average ~41k rows per country).
System is otherwise idle; no significant concurrent workload during the observed slow query.
Buffer pool may not fully cache the 13.7M-row index, causing I/O on first run.
country_name is effectively unique per country_code (common in dimensions), though not enforced.

parameters.query: SELECT c.country_name AS country_name FROM statistic_detail s INNER JOIN country_detail c ON (s.country = c.country_code) GROUP BY 1

EXPLAIN shows country_detail scanned via country_name_idx and statistic_detail accessed via ref on country (country_idx or PK prefix).
No lock waits or deadlocks; CPU and I/O used by the single query.
validation_criteria: Reproduced query plan matches: first table country_detail (type=index on country_name_idx), second table statistic_detail (type=ref on index with key_len ~length of country), Extras show Using index/Using where.
Slow query log shows rows_examined in the multi-million range and latency approximating the reported 30s on similar hardware when cache is cold.
Result set cardinality is <=334 rows as expected.
